answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. Validating identity requires staking raw capital: deploying a single node is cheap, but each replica exponentially escalates bonding stakes. The ledger binds each proof like an indelible stroke of an ink quill, while rogue identities are slashed like felled timber across a dense nebula of rogue nodes, forcing exponential capital exhaustion.
